headline: Indonesia And Norway Advance Carbon Trade Projects At COP31 Summit
seoTitle: Indonesia and Norway Carbon Trade Agreement at COP31
metaDescription: Indonesia launched three blue carbon projects and finalized new regulations for marine carbon trading during the COP31 climate summit with Norway.
aiSummaryBullets: Indonesia and Norway have finalized their inaugural carbon trade agreement during the COP31 climate conference.
The Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries introduced Regulation Number 17 of 2026 to manage blue carbon economic instruments.
Three new blue carbon initiatives were launched, with the government aiming to sequester 5.5 million tons of CO2 through these projects.
aiContextParagraph: At the COP31 summit, Indonesia has expanded its involvement in international carbon markets by launching three blue carbon projects designed to sequester an estimated 5.5 million tons of carbon dioxide. To facilitate this development, the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries has enacted Regulation Number 17 of 2026, which establishes a formal framework for managing the economic value of marine and coastal carbon. This regulatory shift is intended to protect vital marine ecosystems while ensuring that local fishing communities and landowners receive economic benefits from carbon trading. Alongside these national efforts, Indonesia solidified its cooperation with Norway through a contract for the first carbon trade agreement. According to government officials, five other nations have also expressed interest in pursuing carbon transactions with Indonesia, signaling a growing international market for the country's coastal climate assets.
whyItIsViral: The development is widely covered by four independent outlets as part of a significant shift in climate policy and international trade at the COP31 summit.
